name: Unimodular gravity is classically equivalent to GR; Lambda becomes an integration constant; it does not solve the cosmological constant problem

published_statement: As restated in arXiv:2603.14718v1 p.2 (verbatim): "Its defining feature is the imposition of a fundamental constraint: the determinant of the spacetime metric is required to remain fixed throughout the manifold, sqrt(-g) = eps_0. This constraint reduces the full diffeomorphism invariance of GR to volume-preserving diffeomorphisms and leads to trace-free field equations in which the cosmological constant does not appear as a free parameter of the action. Instead, the divergence of the traceless field equations yields the relation R_{;nu}/4 = 8 pi G (T^{mu nu}_{;mu} - T_{;nu}/4), (1) which in general allows for a varying Lambda [15, 19]. Only if the conservation of the energy-momentum tensor T^{mu nu}_{;mu} = 0 is additionally imposed does the cosmological constant reduce to a constant of integration, and the full Einstein equations with a fixed Lambda are recovered [14, 19]. This structure implies that Unimodular Gravity and GR, while sharing the same classical field equations under this additional assumption, are known to differ at the quantum and perturbative levels [15, 18, 19]." And on the CC problem (p.2): Smolin [14] "showing that the quantum effective action remains a functional of a unimodular metric and that vacuum energy contributions of the form g^{ab} C decouple from the gravitational dynamics, providing a concrete mechanism addressing the first cosmological constant problem." Field equations (p.5, eqs.12-15): R_mu nu - (R/4) g_mu nu = kappa (T_mu nu - T g_mu nu /4), equivalently G_mu nu + Lambda(R,T) g_mu nu = kappa T_mu nu with Lambda(R,T) = (R + kappa T)/4.
published_hypotheses: H1 (defining): sqrt(-g) = eps_0 fixed, non-dynamical; diffeomorphism group reduced to volume-preserving diffeomorphisms (2603.14718 p.2).
H2 (field equations): only the trace-free part of Einstein's equations, eq.(12), holds (p.5).

H3 (LOAD-BEARING, 'additionally imposed'): conservation T^{mu nu}_{;mu} = 0. Without it eq.(1) 'in general allows for a varying Lambda'; with it Lambda is an integration constant and GR with fixed Lambda is recovered (p.2).

H4 (scope): the equivalence is of the classical field equations; the theories 'are known to differ at the quantum and perturbative levels' (p.2, citing Fernandez Cristobal 2014, Bufalo-Oksanen-Tureanu 2015, Fabris-Alvarenga-Velten 2023); Fabris et al.'s perturbative discriminator operates 'when standard conservation laws are not imposed' (p.2).
H5 (implicit, standard; checked here, not stated in the restatement): Lambda is constant on each CONNECTED component of spacetime, since the result is d_nu Lambda = 0.

rederivation.outcome: 0 FAIL over 13 checks (exact symbolic, sympy 1.14.0; output in rederive/unimodular-gravity-classical-equivalence.out). C1: nabla^mu(R_mu nu - R g_mu nu/4) = d_nu R/4 verified as an identity on the general time-dependent spherical metric diag(-e^{2A(t,r)}, e^{2B(t,r)}, C(t,r)^2, C^2 sin^2) -- hence the trace-free equations imply nabla_nu (R + kappa T)/4 = kappa nabla^mu T_mu nu, the restatement's eq.(1) rearranged (AGREES). C2: G + Lambda g - kappa T is identically the trace-free equation once Lambda := (R + kappa T)/4, matching eq.(15); with nabla.T = 0, Lambda is constant on a connected domain (AGREES). C3 (witness for H3 being load-bearing): flat FLRW dust, trace-free system reduces to one equation kappa rho = -2 dH/dt; with a = t^{1/2}: rho = 1/(kappa t^2) > 0, nabla^mu T_mu t = 1/(2 kappa t^3) != 0, Lambda(t) = -1/(4 t^2), and G_tt + Lambda0 g_tt = kappa T_tt demands Lambda0 = -1/(4t^2), i.e. no constant Lambda works (AGREES with 'in general allows for a varying Lambda'). C4: static wormhole metric of 2603.14718 eq.(2): trace-free system has rank 2 in (rho, p_r, p_t), Einstein system rank 3 (AGREES with the restatement's p.5 count); radial conservation = TOV form; on the trace-free shell d_r Lambda = kappa x TOV, so conservation <=> Lambda constant (AGREES). C5: minimally coupled scalar on the general spherical metric: nabla^mu T_mu nu = (Box phi - V'(phi)) d_nu phi, so Lagrangian matter conserves T on its own shell. later_literature.what: States outright that the equivalence holds 'under this additional assumption' of T^{mu nu}_{;mu} = 0, that the UG system is more underdetermined (2 vs 3 independent static equations), and that UG and GR 'represent genuinely distinct theoretical frameworks' beyond the classical background level; also proves that traversable wormholes in UG still need NEC violation at the throat (so UG buys nothing against the exotic-matter refusal either).

later_literature.what: Semiclassical 2D: absorbing the diffeomorphism anomaly gives semiclassical trace-free (unimodular) gravity; absorbing it into the trace anomaly gives semiclassical Einstein equations; 'Both alternatives give the same gravitational dynamics [17, 18].' Equivalence of dynamics survives into that semiclassical setting.
Cosmological perturbation theory distinguishes GR and UG, with instabilities in UG 'when standard conservation laws are not imposed' -- classical-perturbative, and only off H3.
Formulations of UG that are classically equivalent diverge at the quantum level; unimodular condition enforced only in spatial average in the standard theory.

Path-integral quantisation of the Henneaux-Teitelboim formulation: vacuum energy g^{ab}C decouples -- 'addressing the first cosmological constant problem'. Bears on the tree's boolean UNIMODULAR_SOLVES_CC_PROBLEM = False, not on classical equivalence.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested on THIS result: nothing here is a measurement, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked. The result is a statement about field equations; its content is the identity C1 (contracted Bianchi) plus one hypothesis (H3). That identity is re-derived here exactly and agrees; no later datum can move an identity. What the TREE lacked is not data but a hypothesis: the conservation condition the source itself names as 'additionally imposed'. Having it does not change the conclusion for the tree's use -- for ordinary Lagrangian matter conservation holds on the matter shell (C5), so within the tree's 'classical' scope the equivalence it quotes is exact -- but it does change the statement's reach: UG admits solutions with non-conserved sources and varying Lambda(t) that GR with constant Lambda does not (C3 witness). The CC-problem sub-claim is a matter of interpretation, not data: Smolin's decoupling argument is on one side, the free integration constant (and, named not read, radiative-stability arguments) on the other. Evidence either way: no moved datum; one dropped hypothesis, shown by computation; one flattened contested boolean.
grade_evidence: Holds exactly on a smaller class than the tree states. (a) The source as restated (2603.14718 p.2) makes T^{mu nu}_{;mu} = 0 an ADDITIONAL hypothesis for 'Lambda is an integration constant' and for 'same classical field equations'; the tree (permute.py:149-151, 361-362, 569-571 and the copies at obstruct.py:281-282, index3.py:970-971, CLAIMS.md:1103-1106) drops it. (b) The drop is load-bearing, SHOWN here: the C3 witness (flat FLRW, a = t^{1/2}, dust rho = 1/(kappa t^2) > 0) solves the unimodular equations with nabla.T = 1/(2 kappa t^3) != 0 and Lambda(t) = -1/(4t^2), and solves GR + constant Lambda for no constant. (c) On the class the source names (classical, conserved T) the re-derivation agrees in every step (C1, C2, C4), and C5 shows Lagrangian matter lies in that class, so the tree's USE -- context in obstruct.py's EXPANSION-IS-A-RELABELLING row, whose verdict rests on theta = 3 H_0, not on UG -- is not moved. (d) The CC-problem boolean (permute.py:363) is a contested sub-claim flattened to False; the tree's own prose 'reframes rather than removes' matches the literature's split. Not WRONG: no counterexample to the tree's use exists and none is claimed. Not STANDS: a hypothesis the source names is dropped. Not OPEN: the theorem is closed-form and was machine-checked here, though the classic primaries are read only via restatement.
